parts.title: My mother the fire fighter
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When people ask me what my mother does, I always smile before I answer. She is a fire fighter, and she is the bravest person that I know.

My mother joined the fire brigade twelve years ago. At first, some of her colleagues did not think that a woman could do the job, because it needs so much strength. She trained harder than anyone, and now she is one of the best in her team. She can carry a heavy person on her back and climb a ladder in full uniform.

She works long shifts, sometimes twenty-four hours, and we never know when she will come home. When the alarm sounds at the station, she has only two minutes to put on her boots and jump on the engine. Once, she missed my birthday party because there was a big fire in the town, but she came home in the morning with a present and a cake.

People think that the job is all about fires, but a lot of it is helping in other ways: freeing a cat from a tree or helping people in a flood. My mother says that the best moment is when she sees a scared person come out safely. I hope that, one day, I can be as brave as she is.

questions.prompt: Why did some of her colleagues doubt her at the beginning?
options: They thought she was too young
They believed the job needs great strength
They thought she had not passed the exams
They did not like working with new people
questions.explanation: They did not think that a woman could do the job because it needs so much strength.

questions.prompt: How did she answer their doubts?
options: She talked to the chief officer
She asked for an easier job
She learned to drive the engine faster
questions.explanation: She trained harder than anyone.

questions.prompt: How long does she have to get ready when the alarm sounds?
questions.explanation: She has only two minutes to put on her boots and jump on the engine.

questions.prompt: What did the writer's mother do after missing the party?
options: She gave the guests a ride on the engine
She sent a message from work
She came home with a cake
She phoned a friend to help
questions.explanation: She came home in the morning with a present and a cake.

questions.prompt: What does her mother like best about the job?
options: Helping a frightened person to safety
Freeing a cat from a tall tree
questions.explanation: The best moment is when she sees a scared person come out safely.

parts.title: Staying safe from fire at home
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Every year, hundreds of fires start in people's homes, but most of them could have been prevented. Fire officers give some simple advice. [1] Fit a smoke alarm on every floor and test it once a month.

The kitchen is the most dangerous room. [2] Never leave a pan on the cooker when you go to answer the phone or the door.

Electrical problems are another cause. [3] If a wire looks damaged, ask an adult to replace it, and never use too many plugs in one socket.

It is also important to have a plan. [4] Everybody in the family should know the quickest way out of every room, and where to meet outside.

If a fire starts, do not try to be a hero. [5] Get out, stay out and call the emergency number from a safe place.
sentences: A candle can be pretty, but it should never be left alone.
Many kinds of animals are afraid of smoke.
Most of these happen when someone is cooking and forgets the food.
You should talk about it together a few times a year.
Most of those are found in old buildings.
Check that all the wires and plugs are in good condition.
Fire spreads much faster than most people think.
The first rule is to make sure that you will hear a warning.

gaps.explanation: The first rule is to hear a warning, and the next sentence says to fit a smoke alarm.
Most fires start when someone is cooking and forgets the food, so never leave a pan.
Checking wires and plugs fits the electrical problems and the next sentence about damaged wires.
Talking about the plan together fits the next sentence about everybody knowing the quickest way out.
Fire spreads faster than most people think, so it is better to get out and call.

parts.title: An email about a fire drill
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Hi Anna, We had a fire drill at school this morning, and it was [1] strange! The alarm rang while we [2] a maths test. At first, I thought that it was a joke, [3] everybody started to walk out of the room. We had to leave our bags behind, and I was really worried about my pencil case. It [4] us only four minutes to get outside, and the teachers said that we did very well. After a while, we [5] back to the classroom and finished the test. I am glad that it was only a drill, [6] I would not like a real fire. Write soon! Cara

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: Very strange modifies the adjective directly.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: Past continuous for an action in progress when the alarm interrupted.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: She thought it was a joke, but everybody started to walk: contrast.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: It takes (took) + person + time is the pattern for how long something needs.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: After a while shows a past event.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: She is glad because she would not like a real fire: reason.

parts.title: What to do in an emergency
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: In an emergency, it is important to stay calm. If you see an accident or a fire, you should call the emergency number [1] once. The person on the phone will ask which service you need: the police, an ambulance or the fire brigade. Then, you must say [2] you are, for example the name of the street, and what has happened. Try to speak slowly and clearly, and do not hang up until they tell you [3] put the phone down. While you wait for help, do not go back into a burning building. Stay [4] from the danger and keep other people away, too. If someone is hurt, you can help [5] sitting with them and keeping them warm. When the emergency services arrive, do exactly what they say. They are used [6] difficult situations and know what is best.

gaps.explanation: Say where you are so that help can find you.
Until they tell you to hang up: the infinitive follows tell.
Stay away from the danger: keep a distance.
Help by sitting with them: a method.
Be used to + noun means be accustomed to.

parts.title: Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the open day at Eastfield Fire Station. Here are a few changes. The ladder show was going to be at ten o’clock, as it says on the programme, but our big engine was called out to a farm this morning, so we have moved the show to two in the afternoon. At four there will be a prize draw for the children, and the winner will sit in the driver’s seat. Until then, you can look at the engines, try on a helmet or have a hot drink in the garden. The first aid class starts at eleven in the main hall. Enjoy your day.

question.prompt: When is the ladder show at the open day?
question.explanation: The programme says ten but the show was moved because the engine was called out; four is the prize draw, so the show is at two.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: What a beautiful old fire engine! Is it from the fifties?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Everyone says that, because it looks like the ones in old films. It’s not that old, it isn’t nearly fifty. It’s thirty-five years old, the same age as me.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Is it still used?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Only for parades now. The white one, which is about ten years old, goes out to the real fires.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: And do you like driving the old one?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I love it, but the steering wheel is huge.

question.prompt: How old is the red fire engine?
question.explanation: It looks like an old film engine but is not nearly fifty; the white one is ten years old, and the red one is thirty-five.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Hello, this is Gerda, the manager of Park House. I’m calling about the fire alarm last night. Many of you thought it was caused by a party in flat twelve, because of the loud music, but the music had nothing to do with it. Others said that Mr Lee burnt a pizza again. He did that in May, but last night he was at his sister’s. The fire fighters checked every flat and found that the cooker in flat four was broken, there was a fault in the electric cable and it made smoke. It will be repaired tomorrow. Nobody was hurt. Thank you for waiting outside so calmly.

question.explanation: The party and the pizza were guesses, and Mr Lee was away; the broken cooker in flat four made the smoke.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Why do you wear such heavy clothes, Giacomo? It’s thirty degrees today!

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I know, I sweat a lot. Everyone thinks it’s to keep warm in winter, but we wear them all year. And it’s not for looks, although the children love the helmet.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: So why?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Fire can burn your skin in seconds. The jacket and trousers are made of a special material that doesn’t catch fire. Without them I couldn’t go near the flames.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: That makes sense.

question.prompt: Why do fire fighters wear heavy clothes?
question.explanation: They wear them all year, so not for winter, and not for looks; the special material stops fire from burning the skin.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Gisela, you’ve been at the station for a week. What’s your favourite thing to do?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I tried the ladder on Monday, and the view was great, but my legs shook, so it’s not for me. And I’ve worked in the office, it’s a nice job, but I want to be outside.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: So what would you choose?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: To sit behind the wheel of that enormous red engine with the siren on, and take the team to the fire. I have my driving test next month and then the course for heavy vehicles.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I’m sure you’ll be the best driver.

question.prompt: What would the woman like to do at the fire station?
question.explanation: The ladder frightened her and she wants to be outside the office; her dream is to take the red engine to a fire.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Good morning, class. Our fire practice is on Friday, so please remember where the safety equipment is. The fire blanket used to be by the science lab door, but the lab moved last year, so that corner is empty now. A few of you think it is in the kitchen because cooking is where fires start, but the kitchen has only an extinguisher. The blanket is on the first floor, at the top of the stairs, on the wall next to the window. Please remember that, and walk quickly, don’t run, when the bell rings.

question.prompt: Where is the fire blanket in the school?
options: At the top of the first floor stairs
question.explanation: It used to be by the lab door and the kitchen has only an extinguisher; the blanket is now at the top of the stairs on the first floor.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Did you hear the alarm this morning, Gaia? It sounded like yours.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Yes, it was mine! I was making toast and I went to answer the phone. When I came back, it was a bit dark on the edges, but not black. I thought there would be smoke, but the window was open, so the kitchen was fine. Then the alarm started to beep, so loudly that my neighbour knocked on the door.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Did you turn it off?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Yes, with a tea towel.

question.prompt: What happened when the woman made toast this morning?
question.explanation: The toast was only dark at the edges and there was no smoke; the alarm beeped so loudly that the neighbour knocked.

turns.speaker: m

options: Stay with her for a few days
question.explanation: He will sleep at his brother’s and wants to buy a cooker at once, but she tells him to wait and check his insurance.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Congratulations, Giulia! I heard you passed the fire fighter test!

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Thanks! Honestly, I’m still a bit shocked, but I hoped for it. I studied for months.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: So you’re thrilled?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Mostly relieved. The last week was terrible, I couldn’t eat or sleep. Now I just want to rest. And I’ll miss college, but not very much.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: You deserve it.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Thank you. I think I will sleep for two whole days before the training starts.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: You will have earned it.

question.prompt: How does the woman feel about passing the test?
question.explanation: She hoped for the result and will not miss college much; mostly she is relieved after a terrible last week.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Have you put up the new smoke alarm, Gilberto?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Yes, and I wish I hadn’t. It cost only ten pounds, I’m not complaining about that, and fitting it was easy, I used two screws. But it goes off when I fry an egg. Every time!

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Maybe it’s too near the kitchen.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: It’s in the hall. My wife says it can smell my cooking. I’ll take it down.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Try cooking with the window open first.

question.prompt: Why does the man dislike his new smoke alarm?
question.explanation: The price was low and fitting it was easy; the problem is that it goes off whenever he fries an egg.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Hello, Gwyneira. What brings you to the station? Are you selling something again?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Not today. And I’m not asking for a favour either, although I may later! I want to learn first aid. My son choked on a sweet last month. I didn’t know what to do, and I was so afraid.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: We have a course on Saturday. Four hours, free of charge.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Perfect, put my name down.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Done. See you at nine.

question.prompt: Why does the woman come to the fire station?
question.explanation: She is not selling anything and not asking for a favour; she wants to learn first aid because her son choked.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Galen, you sound terrible. Where are you?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I’m outside my flat. It’s midnight and I’m locked out. The keys are inside, on the kitchen table.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Didn’t you take the bus home? I thought you were late.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I took the last one, thank goodness. And my phone is in my pocket, I’ve called you with it.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I’ll call the landlord. Or you can sleep here.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I’d rather get inside; the landlord has a spare.

options: He has missed the last bus
He is locked out of his flat
question.explanation: He caught the last bus and has his phone; his keys are inside, so he cannot get in.

parts.title: A talk about the fire brigade
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: gwendolyn
turns.text: Good morning, boys and girls. My name is Gerda, and I am a fire officer. I would like to tell you about my job. The fire brigade in our town has fifty fire fighters. That sounds like a lot, but they don’t all work together. At any time, there are only ten at the station, and the others are resting or training at home. When the alarm rings, the first engine leaves in less than two minutes. We practise that all the time. Sometimes the journey takes five minutes, if the fire is on the other side of town, but the engine always leaves fast. What is in the engine? There are ladders, long hoses and strong ropes, and, most important, a tank of water. Some people think we carry foam for every fire, but we use foam only for special fires, for example with oil. Water is the main thing, and we carry enough for about an hour. Fire fighters don’t only fight fires. We also go to schools to give safety talks. Last year we visited twelve schools, and I hope we will come to yours soon. We have also visited hospitals, but only to check the alarms. Of course, you can’t be a fire fighter without being fit. Every morning we exercise in the gym at the station, with running machines and weights. Some people like to swim, there is a pool nearby, but most of us prefer the gym because it is next to the engines. Now, the most important thing I want you to remember. In an emergency, you dial nine nine nine. Say it with me. Nine nine nine. In some countries it’s one one two, but in our country it’s nine nine nine. Stay calm and give your address. Thank you for listening, and now you can ask me anything.

gaps.explanation: Only ten are at the station at any time, but the brigade has fifty fire fighters.

gaps.prompt: The first engine leaves the station in under ___ minutes
gaps.explanation: A long journey can take five minutes, but the engine leaves in less than two.

gaps.prompt: Besides ladders, hoses and ropes, an engine carries a tank of
gaps.explanation: Foam is only for special fires; the most important thing in the engine is the tank of water.

gaps.prompt: Besides fires, they visit children to give safety talks at
gaps.explanation: They also visited hospitals, but only to check alarms; the safety talks are at schools.

gaps.prompt: For training every morning, they use the
gaps.explanation: Some like to swim in the nearby pool, but most prefer the gym at the station.

gaps.prompt: In an emergency, people should dial 99 and then
gaps.explanation: In some countries the number is one one two, but here it is nine nine nine.

parts.title: An interview with an ambulance driver
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Gaspar, you drive an ambulance. How long is a normal shift?

turns.speaker: d
turns.text: People often think it’s eight hours, like an office job, and I used to work ten hours when I started. But now we do twelve hours, with a few short breaks. We start at seven in the morning and finish at seven in the evening, or the other way round at night.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: That’s long. What happened last week?

turns.speaker: d
turns.text: Oh, last week was special. We didn’t have an accident, thank goodness. A call came from a school, but it was only a child with a sore arm. The real surprise was a baby. A woman was on her way to hospital, but the baby was in a hurry. It was born in the back of the ambulance, with the paramedic helping. It was a girl, and I cried a little.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the hardest part of the job for you?

turns.speaker: d
turns.text: Staying calm. When a family is panicking, and shouting, and someone is badly hurt, I have to be the quiet one. Driving fast through traffic is stressful, but I’ve done it for years, so it’s not new. And I’m used to working at night. The difficult thing is to stay calm when everybody around me isn’t.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: How do you relax after a hard shift?

turns.speaker: d
turns.text: I’m not a great cook, my wife does the cooking. And I love books but I fall asleep after two pages. What I really love is playing football with my two sons in the park. It clears my head, and they think I’m a hero, even if I’m not very good.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What should drivers do when they hear a siren?

turns.speaker: d
turns.text: Don’t stop in the middle of the road, please. That is the worst thing, because we can’t pass. And don’t drive more slowly than normal, either. The best thing is to move over carefully, to the side, and let us pass. Signal, and don’t make sudden moves.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you enjoy most about the job?

turns.speaker: d
turns.text: It’s not the money, of course, and I certainly don’t enjoy the long hours, though I like days off. The best moment is when I get a card from a family that says thank you. I keep them all in a box at home. Last month a little boy drew me a picture of the ambulance. I’ll never throw it away.

questions.prompt: How long is Gaspar's shift now?
questions.explanation: Eight hours is what people think and ten hours was his old shift; now he works twelve.

A call came from a school
questions.explanation: There was no accident and the school call was a sore arm; a baby was born in the back of the ambulance.

questions.prompt: Why is staying calm the hardest part for Gaspar?
questions.explanation: He is used to driving fast and to working at night; the difficult thing is to be calm when everybody else is panicking.

questions.prompt: What does Gaspar do to relax?

questions.prompt: What should people do when they hear a siren?
